suggested_requirements.text: The Framework must capture information from the software tools specified in Table 3.10.3-A.
The Framework must store captured data in a centralized data store.
The user must be able to view the information in the central store in a hierarchical manner.
The Framework must include a browser capable of displaying the information hierarchy.
The Framework must leave a residue on the data store when information is archived to removable media.
The Framework must inform the user that an entity has been archived when the user attempts to access it.
The Framework API must allow client processes to create, delete, and modify entities and entity groups.
The Framework API must allow client processes to create, delete, and modify relationships between entities.
The Framework API must allow client processes to list and access entities.
The Framework API must allow client processes to execute queries for the retrieval of entities.
The Framework must provide a GUI for the user to specify relationships between disparate entities.
The Framework should run on systems with 256 megabytes of RAM.
The Framework Shell should not utilize more than 40 megabytes of RAM.
The mean time between failures (MTBF) shall exceed 3 months.
The Framework must guard against malicious scripts on remote websites from accessing its information.
The Framework must guard against unintended corruption of information by the user.
Any coding conventions used during implementation must be documented and strictly adhered to.
The website for distributing the project shall include provisions for users to make comments and compile a wish-list of features.
The system shall conform to ISO 10646 (Unicode UTF-8) standards for character set encoding.
The system shall conform to Windows 2000 Logo Requirements.
The Framework must be licensed under the GNU Library General Public License (LGPL).
The browser and tools released alongside the Framework must be licensed under the GNU Public License (GPL).
